extra_vocab.en: full of oil or fat, so it feels or tastes heavy
extra_vocab.note: 多半用在餐廳評論與食堂情境，形容食物太油，語氣偏負面。也可形容沾滿油的手、地板或設備。

example.en: The fried chicken here is greasier than at the other shop.
example.zh: 這裡的炸雞比另一家店更油膩。

example.en: It was the greasiest burger on the whole menu.
example.zh: 那是整份菜單裡最油膩的漢堡。

example.en: Our company cafeteria serves less greasy food than before.
example.zh: 我們公司的自助餐廳供應的食物比以前不油膩。

example.en: A greasy smell filled the office after lunch.
example.zh: 午餐後，辦公室裡充滿了油膩的味道。

example.en: Please wipe the greasy fingerprints off the glass door.
example.zh: 請把玻璃門上油膩的指紋擦掉。

examples.en: The service was fast, but the fries were too greasy.
examples.zh: 服務很快，但薯條太油了。

examples.en: Many employees asked for fewer greasy dishes at the cafeteria.
examples.zh: 許多員工要求食堂減少油膩的菜色。

examples.en: The kitchen floor was greasy, so staff wore non-slip shoes.
examples.zh: 廚房地板很滑膩，所以員工穿了防滑鞋。

confusable.diff: greedy 是「貪心的」，拼法相近，但和油膩無關。

example.en: A greedy supplier raised prices twice this year.
example.zh: 一家貪心的供應商今年漲價兩次。

similar.diff: oily 只說明含油或有油，語氣較中性；greasy 通常帶著「太油、不舒服」的感覺。

example.en: The oily sauce stained the tablecloth.
example.zh: 油油的醬汁弄髒了桌布。

similar.diff: fatty 指食物含脂肪多，常用在健康與飲食建議；greasy 強調吃起來的油膩感。

example.en: Doctors advise us to eat less fatty food.
example.zh: 醫生建議我們少吃高脂肪的食物。

example.en: The restaurant is known for its fried fish.
example.zh: 這家餐廳以炸魚聞名。

example.en: Let us meet in the cafeteria at noon.
example.zh: 我們中午在員工餐廳碰面吧。

derived.link: 最基礎的字；grease + -y 變成形容詞「油膩的」，像 salt → salty
greasy + -ness，形容詞變名詞，像 kind → kindness

senses.en: having too much oil or fat
senses.distinguish: 前後文有 food、fries、burger 時，指食物太油。

example.en: The pizza was so greasy that the box turned soft.
example.zh: 這個披薩太油，連紙盒都變軟了。

senses.en: covered with oil, so it feels slippery
senses.distinguish: 前後文有 hands、floor、tools 時，指物體表面沾了油。

example.en: Wash your greasy hands before you touch the keyboard.
example.zh: 碰鍵盤之前，請先洗掉手上的油。

extra_vocab.zh: 定價過高的、貴得不值的
extra_vocab.en: costing more than it is worth
extra_vocab.note: 常見於評論、採購與比價情境，表示價格高過它應有的價值，語氣是批評。不等於單純的「貴」，重點是「不值這個價錢」。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: overpriced 是形容詞，可放在名詞前或 be 動詞後；比較時用 more overpriced，不說 overpricedder。

example.en: Several customers said the hotel breakfast was grossly overpriced.
example.zh: 幾位顧客表示這間飯店的早餐貴得離譜。

collocations.zh: 以得到的東西來說太貴

example.en: The tour package felt overpriced for what you get.
example.zh: 以你得到的內容來說，這個旅遊方案太貴了。

example.en: The new model seems overpriced compared with similar products.
example.zh: 和類似產品相比，新型號似乎定價過高。

examples.en: Most reviewers called the coffee machine overpriced and hard to use.
examples.zh: 大多數評論者說這台咖啡機太貴又難用。

examples.en: We rejected the offer because the parts were overpriced.
examples.zh: 因為零件定價過高，我們拒絕了這個報價。

examples.en: Some members think the conference tickets are overpriced this year.
examples.zh: 有些成員認為今年的研討會門票太貴。

confusable.diff: overpaid 是「薪水或款項付得太多」，主詞是人；overpriced 是東西的價格太高。

example.en: The report says some managers are overpaid.
example.zh: 報告指出有些經理的薪水過高。

similar.diff: expensive 只說價格高，不一定不值得；overpriced 表示價格超過價值。

example.en: The system is expensive, but it saves us time.
example.zh: 這個系統很貴，但能幫我們省時間。

similar.diff: overcharged 是被多收了錢（動作或結果）；overpriced 是定價本身偏高。

example.en: We were overcharged for shipping on the last order.
example.zh: 上一筆訂單的運費被多收了。

example.en: Customers care about value as much as price.
example.zh: 顧客對價值的重視不亞於價格。

example.en: We offer a ten percent discount on bulk orders.
example.zh: 大量訂購我們提供九折優惠。

derived.link: over-（過度）+ price（定價），像 overwork、overtime 的 over-
under-（低於）+ priced，和 over- 相反

extra_vocab.en: good enough that waiting for it is fine
extra_vocab.note: 多用在餐廳、產品上市、服務與活動的評論，表示雖然等了很久，但結果很值得。語氣正面，常放在句尾當結論。
extra_vocab.pattern: N / It + is / was + worth the wait
extra_vocab.grammar_note: worth 後面接名詞或 V-ing，不接 to V：worth the wait、worth waiting；不能說 worth to wait。

examples.en: The line was long, but the food was worth the wait.
examples.zh: 排隊很久，但餐點值得等待。

examples.en: The new phone arrived late, but it was worth the wait.
examples.zh: 新手機雖然晚到，但值得等待。

examples.en: Thank you for your patience. We believe the upgrade is worth the wait.
examples.zh: 感謝您的耐心。我們相信這次升級值得等待。

examples.en: Our fresh bread is worth the wait, so please order early.
examples.zh: 我們的新鮮麵包值得等待，所以請提早訂購。

similar.diff: worth it 範圍更廣，可指金錢、努力、時間；worth the wait 專指等待。

example.en: The extra training cost was worth it for the team.
example.zh: 額外的訓練費用對團隊來說很值得。

similar.diff: worth the effort 強調付出的力氣值得，不一定是等待。

example.en: Writing a clear report is worth the effort.
example.zh: 寫一份清楚的報告是值得花力氣的。

confusable.diff: worthwhile 是單獨使用的形容詞「值得的」，後面不接受詞。
confusable.usage: worthwhile 是形容詞，單獨使用，如 a worthwhile trip；worth 後面一定要接名詞或 V-ing，如 worth the trip。

example.en: Joining the workshop was worthwhile for the whole team.
example.zh: 參加工作坊對整個團隊來說都很值得。

extra_vocab.en: to write each thing on a list one by one
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於帳單、報帳、預算與報價情境，要求把費用或項目一項一項分開寫清楚。常用被動或分詞 itemized 修飾名詞，如 an itemized bill。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: itemize 是及物動詞，直接接受詞：itemize the costs，不加 of；當形容詞用 itemized。

example.en: The statement itemizes every charge from the past month.
example.zh: 這份對帳單逐項列出過去一個月的每筆費用。

example.en: The accountant itemized all travel expenses for the audit.
example.zh: 會計為了稽核，逐項列出了所有差旅費用。

example.en: Itemizing each cost makes the budget easier to check.
example.zh: 逐項列出每筆成本，讓預算更容易檢查。

example.en: Please itemize your expenses before sending the claim form.
example.zh: 寄出請款單之前，請逐項列出你的費用。

example.en: The client asked for an itemized invoice with unit prices.
example.zh: 客戶要求附有單價的逐項明細發票。

example.en: Attach an itemized list of the office supplies you need.
example.zh: 請附上你需要的辦公用品逐項清單。

examples.en: Employees must itemize every meal when they submit a claim.
examples.zh: 員工提出報帳時，必須逐項列出每一餐。

examples.en: Could you itemize the repair costs in your quotation?
examples.zh: 你可以在報價單裡逐項列出維修費用嗎？

examples.en: The finance team will itemize the budget by department.
examples.zh: 財務團隊會依部門逐項列出預算。

confusable.diff: summarize 是把內容濃縮成重點；itemize 是不省略地一項一項列出。

example.en: Please summarize the report in three short points.
example.zh: 請用三個簡短重點摘要這份報告。

similar.diff: list 是比較廣的「列出」，不一定要細分；itemize 強調每項分開、通常含金額。

example.en: Please list the names of all attendees.
example.zh: 請列出所有出席者的姓名。

similar.diff: break down 是把總數拆成細項說明，常和 into 連用；比 itemize 口語。

example.en: Can you break down the total cost for us?
example.zh: 你可以幫我們拆解一下總費用嗎？

example.en: The invoice lists each service and its price.
example.zh: 這張請款單列出了每項服務和價格。

example.en: Travel expense reports are due every Friday.
example.zh: 差旅費用報告每週五要交。

example.en: Keep every receipt for your business trip.
example.zh: 請保留出差的每一張收據。

derived.link: 最基礎的字；item + -ize，變成「做成一項一項」的動詞，像 organ → organize
itemize + -ation，動詞變名詞，像 organize → organization

extra_vocab.en: a company outside your own company that sells goods or services to you
extra_vocab.note: 常見於採購、資訊安全、電商平台與外包情境，指不是自己公司、也不是客戶的另一家外部業者，例如物流、付款或軟體供應商。
extra_vocab.pattern: work with / hire / rely on + a third-party vendor
extra_vocab.grammar_note: third-party 當形容詞時要加連字號，複數只在名詞加 s：third-party vendors；不寫成 thirds-party。

examples.en: We use a third-party vendor to deliver all online orders.
examples.zh: 我們用第三方供應商配送所有網路訂單。

examples.en: Every third-party vendor must follow our data protection rules.
examples.zh: 每家第三方供應商都必須遵守我們的資料保護規定。

examples.en: Several third-party vendors sell their products on our website.
examples.zh: 有幾家第三方供應商在我們的網站上銷售產品。

examples.en: Please send us the contract with the third-party vendor.
examples.zh: 請把與第三方供應商簽的合約寄給我們。

similar.diff: outside supplier 是更口語的說法，意思接近，但沒有「第三方」的法律與合約語氣。

example.en: We buy packaging from an outside supplier in Vietnam.
example.zh: 我們向越南的外部供應商購買包裝材料。

similar.diff: contractor 是承包商，多提供勞務或工程；vendor 是賣東西或服務給你的業者。

example.en: The contractor will finish the office repairs by May.
example.zh: 承包商會在五月前完成辦公室的修繕。

confusable.diff: third party 是名詞「第三方」，沒有連字號；third-party 是形容詞，用來修飾名詞。
confusable.usage: third party 單獨當名詞，如 a third party；放在名詞前面修飾時要寫成 third-party，如 third-party vendor。

example.en: The contract bans sharing data with any third party.
example.zh: 合約禁止與任何第三方分享資料。

extra_vocab.en: the rules about what you can bring into or out of a country
extra_vocab.note: 常見於進出口、貨運、出差與電商情境，說明貨物或行李通關時要遵守的規定，常和 comply with、follow、check 一起出現。
extra_vocab.pattern: comply with / follow / check + customs regulations
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 「海關」的 customs 固定加 s；單數 custom 是「習俗、慣例」。customs regulations 中 customs 不變，regulations 才是複數。

examples.en: All exporters must comply with customs regulations in each country.
examples.zh: 所有出口商都必須遵守各國的海關規定。

examples.en: Please check the customs regulations before you bring samples abroad.
examples.zh: 帶樣品出國前，請先確認海關規定。

examples.en: The shipment was delayed because of new customs regulations.
examples.zh: 這批貨因為新的海關規定而延誤。

examples.en: Our agent will explain the customs regulations by email today.
examples.zh: 我們的代理商今天會用電子郵件說明海關規定。

similar.diff: import rules 只涵蓋進口的規定；customs regulations 同時涵蓋進出口與通關程序。

example.en: The import rules changed for food products last month.
example.zh: 食品類產品的進口規定上個月改了。

similar.diff: customs requirements 強調要準備的文件或條件；customs regulations 指規定本身。

example.en: Please read the customs requirements before you ship the goods.
example.zh: 出貨前請先閱讀海關要求。

confusable.diff: customs duties 是要繳的關稅（費用）；customs regulations 是通關的規定。

example.en: Customs duties depend on the type of goods.
example.zh: 關稅取決於貨物的種類。

extra_vocab.zh: 光顧；以高人一等的態度對待
extra_vocab.en: to use a shop or service often, or to treat someone as if they know less than you
extra_vocab.note: 接店家或餐廳時是正式用語「光顧」；接人時是負面意思，表示用居高臨下的態度對待對方，如 Don't patronize me。受詞是什麼，決定它是哪個意思。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: patronize 是及物動詞，後面直接接受詞：受詞是店家或餐廳時指「光顧」，受詞是人時指「瞧不起、居高臨下對待」。

example.en: Our director often patronizes the small bakery near the station.
example.zh: 我們主任常光顧車站附近的小麵包店。

example.en: Several junior staff felt patronized by the senior manager.
example.zh: 有幾位資淺員工覺得被資深經理瞧不起。

example.en: Many tourists are patronizing the new shops near the harbor.
example.zh: 許多遊客正光顧港口附近的新商店。

example.en: His patronizing tone upset the new employees.
example.zh: 他居高臨下的語氣讓新進員工很不舒服。

example.en: We encourage staff to patronize local businesses during the trip.
example.zh: 我們鼓勵員工在旅途中光顧當地商家。

example.en: Avoid a patronizing tone when you reply to customers.
example.zh: 回覆顧客時，請避免使用居高臨下的語氣。

example.en: Business travelers often patronize a restaurant near their hotel.
example.zh: 出差的人常光顧飯店附近的餐廳。

examples.en: Many office workers patronize the cafe next to our building.
examples.zh: 許多上班族光顧我們大樓旁的咖啡館。

examples.en: Please don't patronize me. I understand the contract terms.
examples.zh: 請不要瞧不起我，我了解合約條款。

examples.en: Agents should explain the policy without patronizing the customer.
examples.zh: 客服人員解釋政策時，不應該對顧客擺出高高在上的態度。

confusable.diff: flatter 是為了討好而說好聽話；patronize（對人）是態度高高在上，把對方當成不懂的人。

example.en: He tried to flatter the client to win the deal.
example.zh: 他想靠奉承客戶來談成這筆生意。

similar.diff: talk down to 是口語說法，意思接近 patronize 的第二義，專指說話時居高臨下。

example.en: Managers should never talk down to new staff.
example.zh: 主管絕不應該用居高臨下的態度對新進員工說話。

similar.diff: shop at 是日常說法，等於 patronize 的第一義「光顧」，但沒有正式感。

example.en: Many families shop at the market on weekends.
example.zh: 許多家庭週末都會到這個市場購物。

example.en: Every customer receives a small gift with the order.
example.zh: 每位顧客的訂單都會附贈一份小禮物。

example.en: We will meet the client at ten tomorrow.
example.zh: 我們明天十點要和客戶見面。

example.en: Loyal customers get early access to every sale.
example.zh: 忠實顧客可以提早參加每一次特賣。

derived.link: 最基礎的字；patron + -ize 變成動詞，像 modern → modernize
patron + -age，表示「顧客的行為或支持」，像 usage、package 的 -age

senses.en: to buy things or use services from a shop often
senses.distinguish: 受詞是 store、restaurant、business 時，是這個意思，語氣正式。

example.en: The hotel guests patronize the gift shop in the lobby.
example.zh: 飯店房客會光顧大廳的禮品店。

senses.zh: 以高人一等的態度對待（人）
senses.en: to treat someone as if they know less than you
senses.distinguish: 受詞是人，或句子有 tone、attitude 時，是這個負面意思。

example.en: Don't patronize me; I have handled this account for years.
example.zh: 不要瞧不起我，這個客戶我已經處理很多年了。

extra_vocab.zh: 就這樣，我人在…（講故事時帶出當時的處境）
extra_vocab.en: words used in a story to show what the speaker was doing at that time
extra_vocab.note: 口語敘事的開場或轉折，用來帶出一個尷尬、好笑或戲劇性的場景，後面常接 V-ing、地點或 when 子句。多益書信與文章較少見，但在對談、演講和故事式文章會出現。
extra_vocab.pattern: There I was, + V-ing / 地點 / 狀態, when + 子句
extra_vocab.grammar_note: There I was 的主詞是 I，後面是過去式 was，講的是過去的場景；主詞可換成 he、she、we，如 there we were。

examples.en: There I was, waiting at the gate, when my flight was canceled.
examples.zh: 那時我正在登機口等候，航班卻被取消了。

examples.en: There I was, ready to present, and my laptop would not start.
examples.zh: 那時我準備好要簡報，筆電卻怎麼都開不了機。

examples.en: There I was, in a new suit, and the office was empty.
examples.zh: 那時我穿著新西裝，辦公室裡卻一個人也沒有。

examples.en: There we were, one hour before the launch, with no samples.
examples.zh: 那時距離發表會只剩一小時，我們卻沒有樣品。

similar.diff: picture this 是請聽眾「想像一下」這個場景，通常用現在式；there I was 是直接講自己過去的經歷。

example.en: Picture this: forty customers waiting and no staff at the door.
example.zh: 想像一下：四十位顧客在等，門口卻沒有人員。

confusable.diff: here I am 說的是現在此刻的狀態；there I was 是敘述過去發生的場景。

example.en: Here I am, ready to start the first session.
example.zh: 我來了，準備好開始第一場會議。
